title: Cohomology of RHom(M,-) is Hom in the derived category, compatibly with connecting maps
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with enough injectives [def-sp-injective-resolutions], let $M$ be an object of $\mathcal A$, let $v=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M,-):\mathcal A\to\mathrm{Ab}$ (left exact and additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive]) and let $Rv:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathrm{Ab})$ be its right derived functor [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], computed on $X$ by a quasi-isomorphism $\varepsilon:X\to I$ to a bounded below complex of injectives as $Rv(X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M,I^\bullet)$ [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. Then for every $X\in D^+(\mathcal A)$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$ there is an isomorphism $\psi^n_X:H^n(Rv(X))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(M[0],X[n])$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], sending the class of a cocycle $f:M\to I^n$ (read as a morphism of complexes $M[0]\to I[n]$) to $(\varepsilon[n])^{-1}\circ f$, independent of the choice of $I$ and natural in $X$. Moreover, for every distinguished triangle $X\to Y\to Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1]$ of $D^+(\mathcal A)$, with $\delta^n:H^n(Rv(Z))\to H^{n+1}(Rv(X))$ the homology connecting maps [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] of the distinguished triangle $Rv(X)\to Rv(Y)\to Rv(Z)\to Rv(X)[1]$, one has $\psi^{n+1}_X\circ\delta^n=(w[n]\circ-)\circ\psi^n_Z$, where $w[n]\circ-:\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(M[0],Z[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(M[0],X[n+1])$ is the connecting map of the homological functor $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(M[0],-)$ [lem-sp-long-exact-of-triangle].
